challenges.because: The recorded data go further than either candidate. The derived min period at max_ss_100C_1v60 is 10.45 ns, which is above the 10 ns design period. Scaled linearly, setup at 10 ns would be about -0.45 ns at that corner. This is an estimate, not a measurement: IO delay is a percentage of the period and the resizer would act differently, so only a 10 ns run settles it. It still means a 10 ns qualification should be expected to face a setup gap as well as the DRV and antenna residue.

notes: Not reached or not settleable from the archive: (1) The sinks of fanout1023/X and fanout1007/X, their net names, and whether any are diode_2 cells. The final netlist (final/nl), DEF and step-54 RepairAntennas log were not archived (sources.json lists 18 files and none of these), so only reading the final netlist or DEF would settle the diode attribution. (2) Masters of fanout1023 and fanout1007. r01 alone states 'fanout1023 is a clkbuf_8' and 'fanout1007 is a buf_4'. No archived file records either master: final-driver-strength.json lists only fanout901 and _20258_. The names follow OpenROAD resizer 'fanoutN' naming, not this flow's 'fanout_repair_N' naming. This is a disagreement, so I left it for the resolver. (3) The per-corner checks.rpt files exist only as 'Extracted verbatim' excerpts, whose hashes cannot match sources.json. Their counts are corroborated by the hash-verified metrics.json. (4) The cross-design antenna scan found 357 results (cdc_twoclock, counter4, counter4_tinydie, gcd, spm, sram_wrapper) with no antenna value recorded ('unknown'). Those designs never recorded a failure, so this cannot hide a closure, but the scan is not a full audit of the request generator's logic. (5) I did not re-audit the case diagnosis's Liberty Boolean-function and 123150-pin connectivity proof for the driver upsize. (6) I did not check the OpenLane 2.3.10 default IO_DELAY_CONSTRAINT, so whether 25% is a relaxation or a tightening relative to the default is unverified. Disagreements (r01 calling the archive unavailable while r02 read it; net-limit headroom versus flow-code change for fanout; long-wire repair for antenna) were left to the resolver. One piece of evidence bears on them: across passes 2 and 3, each RepairAntennas pushed one or two new nets from 16 or fewer to 17. That is consistent with the case diagnosis's 'moves the coupled repair frontier'.
